newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN says Croat police expel pregnant Mostar woman.
newsitem.headline: UN says Croat police expel pregnant Mostar woman.

text.p: Croat police expelled a heavily pregnant Moslem woman and her husband from their flat in the Croat-held sector of the divided Bosnian city of Mostar on Saturday, the U.N. relief agency reported.

"This was a routine eviction for (Croat-held) west Mostar but the problem is that this woman is nine months pregnant, which I think is a bit too much," Ariane Quentier, spokeswoman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, told Reuters.
Quentier said that although the Moslem couple had been living in a flat in west Mostar for the last six months they did not have a legal right to tenancy.
"This (lack of legal tenancy) certainly does not justify what happened. This was not done through any regular administrative procedure. You don't put someone on the street in one hour," she said.
"It is not up to the police to knock on the door and tell people to leave."
Bosnian Moslems and Croats fought an 11-month war which ended with a U.S.-brokered federation agreement in 1994.
Tensions remain high in the Mostar, where the U.N. reported 77 evictions from the Croat sector of the city in 1996. Eastern Mostar is controlled by Bosnian Moslems.
